clue.text: Violent reaction to support for corporal punishment

parts.note: to back someone is to support them, so support gives back
a lash is a stroke of the whip, a form of corporal punishment

explanation.surface: A public outcry against those who would bring back flogging in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden hostile response, especially one against a political change, is a synonym.

clue.text: Everything considered by the object of one's passion

explanation.surface: Taking the whole picture into account, judged by the person one adores.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on the whole, taking everything into account, and also, in older usage, one's beloved, someone who is everything to a person.

clue.text: Stay calm to avoid the fate of Anne Boleyn

definitions.text: to avoid the fate of Anne Boleyn

explanation.surface: Advice to remain composed, as Henry VIII's beheaded queen could not.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn, second wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded in 1536; the second reading takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means remain composed under pressure; literally, it means not losing one's head on the block.

clue.text: A release from the BBC

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A release from the BBC', gives no definition or wordplay for AUNTIE (the BBC's nickname); 'release' looks like an OCR misread of a word such as 'relation', more than three letters off, and a search found no printed text.

clue.text: Instrument used by drivers as a warning

definitions.text: used by drivers as a warning

explanation.surface: A device motorists sound to warn others on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brass wind instrument, and also the hooter on a car that motorists sound as an alert.

clue.text: Male lecturer is in Germany-the sybarite!

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
the German word for is is ist

explanation.surface: Exclaiming that a male academic living in Germany is a lover of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in Germany' looks like a location but asks for the German translation of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is a self-indulgent lover of luxury and pleasure, a close synonym.

clue.text: Change of rite creates a row

indicators.note: a change of the letters of rite signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Altering a religious ceremony causes a quarrel among the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row in a series of rising rows, as of seats in a stadium.

clue.text: Intend to go into action, despite loss of rank

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the past participle: having suffered a lowering of rank

indicators.note: one word going into another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a deed is an action
to intend is to mean

explanation.surface: A soldier who means to fight on even though he has been demoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lowered in status or dignity is the sense; being reduced in rank is a closely related idea.

clue.text: Start shooting! It gets the house-warming under way

definitions.text: It gets the house-warming under way

explanation.surface: An order to fire, followed by a joke about a party for a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes house-warming literally: lighting the fire in the grate heats the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the order to begin firing guns, and also describes lighting a fire in a hearth without a guard.

clue.text: A shade indecent

explanation.surface: Describing something as slightly improper.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a colour, and also means risqué or smutty, as in a dirty film.

clue.text: Implement employed by the police?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tool is used by the constabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means bring a law or plan into effect, and, read literally, describes someone placed into the police force.

clue.text: Foolish tradition means we'll vote as I'd arranged

indicators.note: the letters of we'll vote as I'd, once arranged, form new words

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a foolish custom says it means the electorate will vote as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstitious belief passed down through folk wisdom is a foolish piece of tradition.

clue.text: Guys who have artistic talent

explanation.surface: Describing some men gifted in the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Guys are ropes, and a painter is the rope used to tie up a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters are mooring ropes on boats, as guys are ropes, and painters are also artists.

clue.text: Drain a small water jug

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an ewer is a large jug for water

explanation.surface: A command to empty a little jug of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' reads as a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground pipe carrying away waste water is a type of drain.

clue.text: Oriental returned to help in a pub

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: returned means the word for help is written backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: An Eastern man came back to work in a public house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AID into DIA, which goes inside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from India comes from the East, so is an Oriental in older usage.

clue.text: Sadly, a young lady without direction

indicators.note: without asks for the letter of the direction to be taken out

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Regretfully, a girl has lost her way.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret, used like unfortunately.

clue.text: Having unlimited power is perfect

explanation.surface: Describing a monarch with total authority as flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler has total authority, and the word also means complete or utter, as in absolute bliss.

clue.text: Namely a toast in honour of humour

parts.note: a toast is raised to someone, as in 'to the bride'
wit is humour

explanation.surface: Specifically, raising a glass to celebrate comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are formal ways of introducing a specific example, that is to say.

clue.text: Coach prepared a lot of little coaches

parts.note: to train is to coach
set means prepared or ready

explanation.surface: A trainer got ready a collection of miniature railway carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' as trainer shifts to coaches as railway carriages in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy railway is a collection of miniature carriages and engines.

clue.text: One engineer died after getting frozen

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CE is civil engineer
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: An engineer perished after catching a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in or turned to ice means frozen, a synonym.

clue.text: Turning around constantly to Jerusalem

parts.note: ever means always, constantly
Sion (Zion) is the hill of Jerusalem, and the city itself in poetic use

explanation.surface: Always looking back towards Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Eversion is the turning of something inside out, a technical word for turning outwards.

clue.text: Translated a scene from a Roman dramatist

indicators.note: translated suggests the letters of a scene are put into another form

explanation.surface: A passage from a play by a Roman author rendered in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger wrote tragedies in first-century Rome.

clue.text: Military men thought to have been saved

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
deemed means thought or judged

explanation.surface: Soldiers were believed to have been rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rescued from sin or danger is to be saved, a synonym.

clue.text: Australian soldier who puts in the spadework

explanation.surface: An Aussie soldier who does the hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian and New Zealand soldiers are nicknamed diggers, and literally a person who excavates with a spade.

clue.text: Notable description of the Star of Bethlehem

definitions.text: description of the Star of Bethlehem

explanation.surface: A notable described as the star that guided the Magi.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star of Bethlehem led the Magi to Jesus, so it was literally a guiding light.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent person is a prominent figure, and the Star of Bethlehem was a light that guided the wise men.

clue.text: A woman unmoved by set-backs

indicators.note: a word unchanged when its letters are set back to front reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A resilient woman not affected by misfortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-backs' looks like misfortunes but means being written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, standing for a woman.

clue.text: Plenty are drawn into random selection

explanation.surface: Many people are picked in a random draw.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a great many, and also tokens drawn to decide something by chance.

clue.text: A hazy reflection in the centre

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word for hazy is read backwards

parts.note: dim means hazy or faint

explanation.surface: A faint image of oneself in a mirror at the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in the middle of or surrounded by, a synonym.

clue.text: Housing Englishmen under canvas

indicators.note: Englishmen under canvas are inside the tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, so under canvas means in a tent
E for English plus men

explanation.surface: Accommodating men from England in tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, a form of housing.

clue.text: He started out as a private cloth worker

definitions.text: He started out as a private

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woven cloth
a worker ant, the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A textile labourer who began his career as an ordinary soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A private is the lowest army rank, and a sergeant usually rises from it.
explanation.definitionFit: This non-commissioned officer rank is normally reached by promotion from the ranks of ordinary soldiers.
